definition: The process by which a material or surface reduces the energy of sound waves, minimizing reflections and reverberation.
Background sound present in a recording environment, which can affect the clarity and quality of a recording.
Acoustic treatment designed to absorb low-frequency sound waves to control bass buildup in a room.
A stereo microphone technique using two figure-8 microphones placed at 90 degrees to each other to capture a realistic stereo image.
A microphone with a heart-shaped polar pattern that primarily picks up sound from the front and rejects sound from the rear.
